intro: This branch turns trigonometry into functions that work for any angle, not just those inside a triangle. Their wave-shaped graphs describe repeating patterns such as tides, Ferris wheels and daylight, and a few skills include short proofs where the learner picks the reason for a step.

V.9.01.what: Drawing an angle on a grid as a turn that starts from the positive x-axis (standard position). This lets angles be any size, even negative or more than a full turn.

levels.a: Picks the picture that shows an angle correctly drawn from the positive x-axis.
levels.b: Knows positive angles turn counterclockwise and negative ones clockwise, and says where the turn ends.
levels.c: Reads angles of more than a full turn from a picture, such as two turns and a bit.
levels.d: Names which quarter of the grid (quadrant) an angle ends in, in degrees or radians.

V.9.02.what: Coterminal angles end in the same place, like 30 degrees and 390 degrees, because they differ by whole turns.

levels.a: Finds a matching angle by adding or subtracting 360 degrees.
levels.b: Does the same in radians (another unit for angles), adding or subtracting 2 times pi.
levels.c: Finds the smallest positive angle that ends in the same place, sometimes adding several turns.
levels.d: Picks the general rule that lists every angle ending in the same place.

V.9.03.what: Using a circle of radius 1 (the unit circle) to define sine and cosine for any angle. Cosine is a point's left-right position on it and sine is its up-down position.

levels.a: Reads cosine as the left-right position and sine as the up-down position of a point.
levels.b: Finds tangent by dividing the up-down position by the left-right one.
levels.c: Picks the reason for a step in a short proof that this agrees with right-triangle trigonometry.
levels.d: Finds the missing coordinate of a point on the circle exactly, using its quadrant.

V.9.04.what: Learning the exact sine, cosine and tangent values for the most common angles all the way around the circle.

levels.a: Gives exact values for 30, 45 and 60 degrees.
levels.b: Gives the values where the circle crosses the axes, including when tangent is undefined.
levels.c: Finds exact values for common angles anywhere around the circle.
levels.d: Recalls the common values by heart, judging true-or-false statements in degrees and radians.
levels.e: Works out an expression that combines several special angles at once.
levels.f: Adds up a long list of values quickly by pairing terms that combine to make 1.

V.9.05.what: A reference angle is the sharp angle between an angle's ending side and the x-axis. It lets any angle be worked out from a familiar small one.

levels.a: Finds the reference angle for an angle in any quarter of the grid.
levels.c: Uses a reference angle and the quarter to find an exact trig value.
levels.d: Handles negative angles and angles of more than a full turn.

V.9.06.what: Knowing whether sine, cosine and tangent are positive or negative in each quarter of the grid.

levels.a: Says whether a given ratio of an angle is positive or negative.
levels.b: Uses the memory trick "All Students Take Calculus" to recall the signs.
levels.c: Works out which quarter an angle is in from the signs of two ratios.
levels.d: Finds the other ratios exactly from just one of them and the quarter.

V.9.07.what: Finding trig values for any angle from a point on its ending side, even if the point is not on the unit circle.

levels.a: Finds a ratio from a point's coordinates and its distance from the center.
levels.b: Works out that distance first using Pythagoras, then finds a ratio.
levels.c: Gives exact answers with square roots rather than decimals.
levels.d: Handles points on an axis, where a ratio may be zero or undefined (dividing by zero).

V.9.08.what: Drawing the graphs of sine and cosine, which are smooth repeating waves.

levels.a: Uses a point moving around the unit circle to tell whether the graph rises or falls.
levels.b: Reads key points from the graph: highs, lows and zero crossings.
levels.c: Answers questions about one or more full cycles (periods), such as how many peaks.
levels.d: Explains that the sine wave is the cosine wave shifted sideways.

V.9.09.what: Changing a wave's height (amplitude) and how long it takes to repeat (period).

levels.a: Reads the amplitude from the number in front, knowing a minus sign only flips the wave.
levels.b: Finds the period from the number multiplying x inside.
levels.c: Reads the amplitude and period from a graph.
levels.d: Writes the equation of a wave from its graph.
levels.e: Counts how many times a wave reaches a given height in a stretch, including never.
levels.f: Finds how often a sum of two different waves repeats.

V.9.10.what: Sliding a wave sideways (phase shift) or up and down (moving the middle line it rises and falls around).

levels.a: Reads which way and how far a wave is shifted sideways.
levels.b: Finds the middle line and the highest and lowest values.
levels.c: Handles a wave with all changes combined, tidying the inside to read the shift correctly.
levels.d: Writes the full equation of a wave from its graph.
levels.e: Rewrites a flipped wave as an unflipped one shifted sideways.
levels.f: Finds every sideways shift that turns one wave exactly into another.

V.9.11.what: Using sine and cosine waves to model real repeating patterns.

levels.a: Models the rise and fall of ocean tides from high and low tide times.
levels.b: Models the height of a seat on a Ferris wheel over time.
levels.c: Models hours of daylight through the year.
levels.d: Fits a wave equation to a table of data.

V.9.12.what: Drawing the graph of tangent, which repeats but shoots off to infinity at regular gaps.

levels.a: Lists the asymptotes, the vertical lines the graph approaches but never touches.
levels.b: Finds the period, knowing tangent repeats every pi rather than every 2 pi.
levels.c: Finds key values on the graph, including where it is undefined.
levels.d: Finds the period and asymptotes of a stretched or flipped tangent graph.

V.9.13.what: Cosecant, secant and cotangent are 1 divided by sine, cosine and tangent. Their graphs come from the graphs of those three.

levels.a: Finds exact cosecant values as 1 divided by sine.
levels.b: Finds exact secant values as 1 divided by cosine.
levels.c: Finds exact cotangent values, even where tangent itself is undefined.
levels.d: Picks the reason for a step in a proof about which values secant can take.

V.9.14.what: Inverse trig functions answer 'which angle has this sine?' To give one answer, each one only returns angles from a set range.

levels.a: Explains why the angles must be limited to get a single answer.
levels.b: Knows the range of angles each inverse function can give.
levels.c: Finds exact values, such as the angle whose sine is one half.
levels.d: Picks the correct graph of an inverse function.

V.9.15.what: Combining a trig function with its inverse, and seeing when they cancel out and when they do not.

levels.a: Simplifies cases where the inverse goes first, which simply cancel.
levels.b: Completes a short proof for the trap where the angle falls outside the allowed range.
levels.c: Draws a right triangle to find the exact value of a mixed combination.
levels.d: Rewrites such combinations as algebra expressions in x, with no trig left.
levels.e: Works out pairs that mix two different functions, such as sine inside an inverse cosine.
levels.f: Finds every x that makes two different inverse functions equal.
